item.description:
Etna 1.7 (build 9)

Summaries no longer need an account or an API key to be good: a local language model, downloaded once, writes your notes entirely on this Mac — including Russian meetings and hour-long calls that Apple Intelligence could not take in one piece.

  • New engine: Local model. Pick it in Settings › Summary (it is the first tile) or during setup; Etna downloads a 3 GB model from Hugging Face, verifies it, and keeps it under Application Support. Summaries run in a separate helper process so a memory-hungry summary can never interrupt a recording, and the helper quits by itself about a minute after the notes land.
  • Longer meetings, fewer stitches: the local model reads up to an hour of transcript in one pass on 16 GB Macs (half that on 8 GB), so decisions and action items are not lost between chunks. Russian and mixed-language meetings summarize locally — Apple Intelligence still cannot.
  • Opt-in for now: nothing is downloaded and no engine is switched until you pick the tile. Apple Intelligence and the cloud engines are unchanged. The local model becomes the suggested free default once it clears the faithfulness bar in our meeting evaluation — a 4B model still reports some open questions as settled, so cloud keys remain the best notes today.
  • If the model is chosen but not ready yet, summaries use Apple Intelligence meanwhile and are written locally once the download finishes — a stored cloud key is never used unless you chose it.
  • Downloads survive quitting, pause on hotspots and during recordings, and can be cancelled, resumed, repaired or deleted from Settings. The disk check keeps the recorder's free-space reserve intact.
  • Housekeeping: the summary-recovery sweep now also picks up meetings whose summary waited for the model; Stop & Save never waits more than 20 seconds on a local summary; Settings › About lists the new model and runtime licenses.

Etna 1.6 (build 8)

Speaker recognition gets substantially more reliable, the notch panel stops blocking clicks on the windows beneath it, and summaries defend themselves against cut-offs.

  • A known voice that sounded nearly identical to another remembered person is now disambiguated and claims its own name instead of staying silent every meeting. A damaged voice-memory store (two people filed under one voiceprint) is detected and repaired on first launch, with a one-time summary card and a one-tap undo for each item. Crosstalk fragments no longer mint phantom speakers: a soft cap flags "extra voice" for review instead. Someone who briefly drops out of live tracking is recognized again rather than restarting as a new "Speaker N". Voice memory keeps learning in large meetings once a name is typed and the audio checks out.
  • Dialogs and windows parked at the top-center of the screen are clickable again while Etna's panel is open. Previously, during onboarding, a hover-opened meeting panel, or the ten-second auto-record countdown, a transparent area around the panel swallowed clicks on whatever sat beneath it (Zoom prompts, permission requests), so they had to be dragged aside first.
  • Summaries that come back cut off or with drifted section headings are detected and retried once instead of being filed as-is, a rare bug that corrupted the splice between a summary and its meeting rollup is fixed, and a summary rebuilt from a saved transcript now matches the meeting-end one.
  • Deleting voice memory now asks first: "Forget everyone", forgetting one person, and "Reset my voice" each confirm what is and isn't affected.
  • Transcript text can be selected and copied once a bubble is finalized.
  • Clearer failure states: the finished card says when the final transcript rewrite failed (speaker names in the file may be stale), an undo that can no longer be applied explains itself, a failed language-model download offers Retry instead of silently listing the language as ready, and the translation download window gains a Close button on failure.
  • Headphone meetings: less common system-audio sample rates are no longer rejected in favor of the tap's claim; daily housekeeping now also clears aged orphan audio left by interrupted offline passes.
  • Settings › About lists the on-device model licenses and attributions.

Etna 1.5 (build 7)

Headphone meetings now transcribe live, and a failed summary is no longer lost — Etna rebuilds it from the saved transcript.

  • Lost summaries recover themselves: when a meeting-end summary fails (network drop, provider outage), the finished card offers "Try Again" — and on the next launch Etna quietly rebuilds summaries for recent meetings whose transcript was saved without one.
  • Remote speech shows up live during headphone meetings: attributed "Speaker N" bubbles appear within moments of someone talking instead of filling in only after Stop, and a warning appears if Etna is hearing a call but capturing no words from it.
  • Speaker naming and attribution no longer drift as a meeting runs long — a clock-rate correction keeps live transcripts aligned with the real audio.
  • AirPods and other Bluetooth headsets: remote voices are no longer garbled into fragments when another app holds the microphone (e.g. Zoom), and system-audio capture recovers cleanly when the output device changes mid-call.
  • The notch level indicator now animates on remote speech too, not just your own voice.
  • A momentary network blip at meeting end no longer costs you the summary — cloud summaries, titles, and classification retry once after a short pause.
